steps.content: The backstage area before the show is more chaotic than you expected. Racks of performance outfits hang in rows, decorative ribbons and balloons are strewn about, and in the middle of the hallway, a large number sticker sits all alone, for whatever reason.

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: Chief, this is your temporary backstage pass. Just hang it around your neck. Though you're from the Bureau, there are a lot of people today. It'd be a hassle if one of the staff stopped you...

steps.speaker: Choice
options: Aren't you one of the staff?

choices.text: Aren't you one of the staff?

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: Not exactly. I just help out pretty often, so I happen to know the ropes.

But the folder in her hands, covered in color-coded sticky notes, tells a different story. Lighting, supplies, flower arrangements, the surprise cake, entry routes—every item is meticulously marked in various colors.
You watch as Evie briskly handles one crisis after another. It's hard to imagine that this is the same girl who was afraid a single cough might take up too much of your time.

steps.speaker: Fan A
steps.content: Evie! The banners just arrived! I'd like to start cutting them right away, but the delivery guy said there are too many boxes, so he can only drop them at the back door. What do we do?

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: The back door? But that's where the equipment goes through later. We can't afford to have it blocked... Let me think, cough cough...
Though she looks ghastly right now, she still does her best to act like a proper organizer and see every last thing through. Seems like she really doesn't want to waste the chance you gave her.

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: ...Have them leave everything by the warehouse entrance for now. Just make sure they don't block the fire exit. Oh, and, get a couple of people over there to move the stuff.

steps.speaker: Fan B
steps.content: Evie, um... I just checked the final payment for the cake, and it looks like it's a bit over budget. Should I send a payment request to the group chat? Get the people online to chip in?

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: It's fine, I'll cover it for now. Everyone's already worked so hard. Let's not let something like this get in the way of today's surprise.

steps.speaker: Fan B
steps.content: We can't just let you cover it all yourself! Today is Mimi-meow's 365th live AND her first anniversary! We absolutely cannot drop the ball! I don't care if I have to live on dirt for a while, I... What the?! How are you so fast, Evie?!

The moment she finishes speaking, Evie lowers her head and makes the transfer on her terminal. The motion is practiced, almost like she's handling payment for office supplies at work, except nobody is ever going to reimburse her for this one. Still, she doesn't spare it a second thought.

steps.speaker: Fan C
steps.content: Right?! No fair, Evie! You always rush to pay and handle all the logistics, and by the time you're done, there's nothing left for us to do! We never even get a chance to show our love for Mimi-meow... Come on, throw us a bone here!

And yet, her <color=#fb9259>sacrifices</color> don't stand out here at all. If anything, it's something to fight over. Perhaps that, more than anything else, is what makes this lively, devoted little group so special.
It becomes even more obvious when you look at the numerous people rushing back and forth—not a single one of them is wearing a staff uniform.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Wait... are all these people fans who volunteered to <color=#fb9259>help</color>?

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: Well, not all of them... Haha. But there are a lot more volunteers than usual today, so the regular staff have basically been swallowed up by the crowd. It's the anniversary live, after all. Everyone wants to see their efforts help Mimi-meow shine <color=#fb9259>brighter</color>!

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: Honestly, I never expected the manager to hand over so much control for this surprise event and just let us fans take the reins... Hehe, it feels great to be trusted. Makes me want to work even harder!
Trust, or exploitation? Ever since you saw the manager's persuasion tactics and learned that he had manipulated Evie into using her power illegally, you've been wary of him and whoever's backing him.

This troubling culture in Mimi-meow's fandom, one where giving beyond their means is seen as a badge of honor, may well be a result of the company deliberately fostering and steering such a mindset for profit.

Of course, you won't point any of that out in front of the believers. For now, the task is to observe and blend in... You need to see whether the star of this show could be the key to changing everything.

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: Sorry, I need to take this... Yes, you got the right place. Is this the cake delivery? The front entrance is for the audience, could you come around to the back... Huh? You ran into the equipment truck? But I don't think anyone's free to go meet up with you right now...
It sounds like Evie has run into a staffing problem. Her eyes sweep back and forth across the bustling crowd in front of her, trying to work out the logistics in her head.

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: But...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Just stay here. You're on medical leave. I can't have you running to the back door and back again. What if you collapse on the way?

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: ...Then I'll leave it to you! Thank you so, so much!
She pulls a sheet from her folder, flips it over, and scrawls out a route in seconds, the instructions already tumbling out of her mouth.

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: Once you get the cake, just bring it here! This is the highlight of our event, so I really can't thank you enough for helping. I'll come meet up with you as soon as I can!
Alley

One look at the cake and you immediately understand what Evie meant by "highlight." Calling it a cake would be an understatement. It's more like a miniature stage model, dressed up in buttercream and icing.

The cake has three tiers in an orange gradient, topped with a fondant figurine of Mimi-meow. Beside it is a glittering plaque that reads: "Happy 1st Anniversary to our idol! For the one and only Mimi-meow!"

steps.speaker: Delivery Person
steps.content: Careful with that. There's dry ice and light strips inside. Apparently, they're supposed to light up when the cake goes on stage.
As the delivery person hands the cart over to you, there's a hint of sympathy in their expression. Looks like they've taken you as a porter.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: First I've heard of a cake that has power.

steps.speaker: Delivery Person
steps.content: Fan support culture is pretty crazy these days. This isn't even that over the top, in fact.
...This isn't over the top? You can't quite hide your disbelief as you silently wheel that saccharine, expensive, and impossibly heavy monument of <color=#fb9259>love</color> into the backstage.

As you do, a question quietly surfaces. If even you, the one merely pushing the cart, feel the weight of it... will the person receiving this surprise really not feel burdened by it? Or are you simply too unfamiliar with fandom culture to understand?
Livehouse Backstage

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: No dents, light strip connector's intact, dry ice is perfect... Thank you so much, Chief!

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: The show's about to start! Could you stay and wait with me a little longer? We're planning to wheel it onto the stage during the fifth song!
After rushing over to check on the cake, Evie stays by your side at the edge of the stage with no intention of moving. You can't help but ask—

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Aren't you going to watch from the front?

The opening announcement from out front signals the start of the show, and the backstage briefly falls quiet. Music pours through the walls and curtains, the beat strong enough to set the decorative lights on the cart trembling.

The cheers from the crowd roll in like a tide of burning emotion. Even from where you stand, far from the best seats, you can feel their passion. Evie stands at the edge of the curtain, her hands clutching the flow chart tightly. Yet, there's a smile on her face.

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: Not today! We managed to keep this surprise secret thanks to the manager's help. Even Mimi-meow doesn't know about it! I have to stay on standby here!

The fact that Mimi-meow has no idea casts a shadow over the question that had formed in your mind earlier, but you don't press further. You simply wait alongside Evie, who can't help swaying gently and singing along to the music, even from back here.
Before long, the moment to reveal the surprise comes.
Stage
The last note fades, and Mimi-meow is already posed for the next song. But the intro doesn't come. She waits half a beat before glancing at the sound booth, puzzled and still catching her breath.
Before the audience can register the pause and start murmuring, the manager strides out from the other side of the stage, microphone in hand.

steps.speaker: Manager
steps.content: Today is a very special day. Three hundred and sixty-five shows. That means, thanks to all your love and passion, we've been able to light up Mimi-meow's stage in this city three hundred and sixty-five times.

steps.speaker: Manager
steps.content: For such a grand occasion, it'd be a real shame to just go through the setlist like usual and call it a night, don't you think?
The crowd finally catches on, and the cheers build steadily, heating the atmosphere up little by little.

steps.speaker: Fans
steps.content: Yeah!!!

steps.speaker: Manager
steps.content: So, today, a group of people who <color=#fb9259>love</color> Mimi-meow more than anything have prepared a gift for her in secret. Mimi-meow, please look to the left side of the stage!
The crowd erupts, while Mimi-meow, caught off guard by the announcement, freezes. She grips the microphone so hard her fingers nearly go white, though she eases her hold not long after and smiles.

That smile is practiced, yet cold. Like a light that switches on the moment it's told to. Does she always smile like that? You glance over at Evie, only to find her so tense with anticipation that she doesn't seem to have noticed anything off at all.

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: I-it's my turn. Alright... I can do this!

Evie takes a deep breath. A flush of color surges up and washes away the pallor of her face. Her body sways as she pushes the cake cart forward, and you instinctively reach out to steady her. Only then do you realize she's already drawing on her power, despite her state.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Evie.

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: I'll... keep it under control, Chief. Please, lend me your strength... even a little is fine!

An orange light rises from her fingertips, tracing along the light strip at the base of the cake cart before spilling across the floor like stars in the night sky, spreading all the way to the center of the stage.
The light is bright but unstable. It trembles and flickers like Mania straining against its shackles. Even so, it makes Mimi-meow shine far more brilliantly than any stage light ever could.

steps.speaker: Fan D
steps.content: It's Evie!!! Look, she's been coughing all night, but her light is still so bright!!! Her <color=#fb9259>love</color> has <color=#fb9259>lit up</color> the whole venue!!!

steps.speaker: Fan E
steps.content: Incredible! She's doing this even when she's sick! You're a legend, a role model, and the gold standard for fans, Miss Mimi-meow! Let's show everyone our <color=#fb9259>love</color> for Mimi-meow!!!

steps.speaker: Manager
steps.content: Look! The light that's shining upon this gift right now isn't powered by electricity—it's powered by <color=#fb9259>love</color>. Mimi-meow, this is everyone's message to you: you have never shone alone on that stage!

The manager's melodramatic speech carries to every corner of the venue through the speakers. Glow sticks rise one after another in the crowd, swaying like a tide. Screams, applause, and Mimi-meow's name pile on top of each other until the stage itself seems to be floating above the clouds.

Evie pushes the cake cart forward along the trail of light, and you can see that her eyes have already gone red. She looks genuinely moved by the miracle she helped create, her footsteps light and unsteady, as if she might drift off the ground.

The harsh orange light cuts across at an angle, partially blocked by the towering decorations and fondant signs. What the audience sees is an idol surrounded by <color=#fb9259>love</color>, but what you see is her face, caught squarely in a sliver of shadow.
Is she really smiling?

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: M-Mimi-meow! Today is your 365th show, and your first anniversary as an idol... so we, cough, cough, we put together these little surprises to show you how grateful we are...
Evie finally manages to push the cake up to Mimi-meow. She picks up the microphone, coughing twice before forcing it back down. She doesn't want even a hint of noise to mar this perfect moment.

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: You've given me, and all of us, so much <color=#fb9259>love</color> and courage. You're the one who lit up our colorless lives and helped us find just a little more strength to carry on. So today... we want to be the ones to give you light.

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: Without you, I don't know if I'd still be here... cough, wait, no, I shouldn't be saying things like that on a day like this! Mimi-meow, all you need to know is that I'll keep supporting you, no matter what!

Her words begin to trail off into a jumble, her voice becoming choked. She laughs it off with an embarrassed smile and pulls herself together, then presents a knife with an orange ribbon tied to its handle.

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: Go on then, Mimi-meow! Make the first cut, and take all our <color=#fb9259>love</color> with it!

steps.speaker: Mimi-meow
steps.content: ...Aren't you going to cut it with me? You put so much thought into this, spent so much money, pushed yourself to use your power for the lights even when you're sick, gave it everything just to stand here... and you won't cut it with me?

steps.speaker: Evie
steps.content: Huh? Me? Of course not. You're the star of today, and you'll always be the star in my heart. Today, the spotlight belongs to you and you alone!

Mimi-meow watches her with heavy eyes, as if a thousand words are lodged in her throat. Beside her, the manager gives her a gentle smile and a nod. Below the stage, countless cameras are on them, all waiting for that perfect, emotional moment to close the night.
And it takes a long while before she finally raises her hand—but not to take the knife. Instead, she reaches for her own microphone.

steps.speaker: Mimi-meow
steps.content: Thank you, everyone. But... I'm sorry. I'm not feeling the best today...
She manages a smile, one that's anything but genuine.

steps.speaker: Mimi-meow
steps.content: We may need to pause the show for a moment... I'm sorry.

She steps back, avoiding the cake cart and the knife still hanging in the air, then turns and walks briskly off the other side of the stage. Meanwhile, Evie only stands there, arm still stretched out, knife in hand, with no idea what to do.

A wave of worried cries erupts from the audience. The manager's smile drops from his face as he turns and hurries after her. Evie remains frozen for a moment, her gaze sweeping past you in search of help. Ultimately, though, she wills herself to follow.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Evie, retract your power first!

You can feel the life force she had barely sustained through sheer emotion draining away, and fast. You curse under your breath as you push through the stage to chase after her, all while working to suppress her rapidly surging Mania.
Livehouse Backstage

By the time you reach her, Evie has already stopped outside the dressing room door. Yet, she doesn't go in. The ribbons she had carefully arranged just hours ago hang in the corridor, trampled into crumpled heaps by the people rushing back and forth.

Every word of the argument spilling out from the dressing room is sharp and piercing, puncturing the dream that had wrapped itself around the entire venue—a dream of idols, light, and <color=#fb9259>love</color>.

steps.speaker: Manager
steps.content: What was that just now? Why'd you walk out on all those fans, just like that?! You think that makes you cool or something?! Have you forgotten what your image is supposed to be? Is that how a bright, bubbly little sun is supposed to act?!

steps.speaker: Manager
steps.content: Those ATMs are easy to milk, but they're not stupid! Do you really think they'll spend even a cent on you if you keep putting on an attitude and disregarding their devotion?! What, do you think you're some superstar?! Without those people out there, you're **** doomed!

steps.speaker: Mimi-meow
steps.content: Sure, I'm not a superstar, but we're business partners! What gives you the right to do all that and hide everything from me?! I never asked for any of this, and I definitely never asked for this shameless promotional scheme!

steps.speaker: Mimi-meow
steps.content: Crowdfunding regardless of their financial situation, demanding volunteer work regardless of their health... Is it fun to exploit my fans like that? Aren't you the least bit afraid of word getting out?! You're basically handing antis what they need on a silver platter!

Mimi-meow's tone is blunt, carrying a firmness completely unlike her approachable persona as an idol. Her every word is laced with biting sarcasm, leaving the manager speechless for a moment. So, he begins to shift tactics, his tone softening as he speaks.

steps.speaker: Manager
steps.content: ...You're right, there are risks, but the returns are just as clear! We don't have an unlimited budget, so I had no other choice. We want to make your little dream come true too... what was it again... right, to bring love and hope to more people!

steps.speaker: Manager
steps.content: The flower walls, the ribbons, the whole venue... Someone else took care of all of it. Isn't that great? And the thing is, they loved every second of it! Just look at Evie! She's coughing her lungs out and was still smiling as she handed you that knife. This is exactly what the people want to see!

steps.speaker: Manager
steps.content: Look, I've got a heart too. Truth be told, the reason I agreed this time was because I was genuinely touched when they proposed doing something special, Mimi-meow. Why on earth would you turn away this <color=#fb9259>love</color> that's being handed right to you?

Throughout this exchange, soaked in cold calculation, Evie has kept her head down and endured. And yet, the manager's sugar-coated words are enough to make her look up again. She's waiting for a word of approval from Mimi-meow, her eyes gleaming with hope.

steps.speaker: Mimi-meow
steps.content: <color=#fb9259>Love</color>? You call blindly sacrificing all that someone has, without thinking about whether they can actually handle it, "love"? That's nothing but <color=#fb9259>self-gratification</color>!
But the voice from inside the dressing room only shatters the last bit of illusion she has left. Mimi-meow's cold words land like arrows, pinning her to the spot.

steps.speaker: Mimi-meow
steps.content: If this is what <color=#fb9259>love</color> looks like, then I don't want it, nor can I afford it. Don't do anything like this again. You're only putting me in a difficult position.
Days of preparation, a surprise arranged under enormous strain—all of it, in this very moment, has been reduced to a joke in front of a product manufactured by money.
...Has your worst fear come true? Is this just another idol who sees her fans as nothing but a meal ticket? Your heart sinks as you turn to look at Evie.

Her reaction, however, is smaller than you expected. She simply lowers her head again, slowly, eyes falling to the cake knife still in her hand. It's as if she's only now realizing that what the delicate little thing has faced was never a rejection. It was never taken at all.

The emotions on the other end of the shackles drain away all at once, leaving behind nothing but a hollow, plummeting coldness. The excitement and anticipation that had kept her shining on that stage moments ago are being ground to dust by a simple statement: "Don't do anything like this again. You're only putting me in a difficult position."

You reach out, hoping to pull her out of the spiral of negativity for even a moment, only to realize she's still forcing a smile. She looks up at you, lips parting, as if she's trying to tell you she's fine.
But before she can voice a single syllable, her frail body sways once, twice, like a marionette whose strings have been cut, and she crumples to the ground, her face drained of all color.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Evie!
You barely manage to catch her. The fabric of her suit, soaked in cold sweat, clings to your palms, clammy and uncomfortable. It makes the summer heat outside feel like a lie.

There's no time to blame anyone. You curse yourself for having underestimated just how much discomfort Evie was willing to hide and endure for the sake of supporting Mimi-meow. You yank out your terminal and make an emergency call to the Bureau's medical team.

steps.speaker: Manager
steps.content: What is going on?! Why is she here? And you—

The commotion outside has cut the argument short, and Mimi-meow comes rushing along with the manager. The manager recognizes Evie, who's collapsed in your arms, and for a moment, his anger falters, only to give way to annoyance.

steps.speaker: Manager
steps.content: Don't tell me Mimi-meow actually called it? We've barely made any returns, and now she's messing everything up... Tch, the crowd's still out there. Do not let them know!

steps.speaker: Choice
options: Oh, you don't need to worry about that.

choices.text: Oh, you don't need to worry about that.

steps.content: Mimi-meow stands behind him, her makeup still immaculate. It's a mask for her to conceal every flicker of emotion, yet right now, it fails to hide the faint redness rimming her eyes. For a moment, it seemed like she wanted to take a step forward. But she stops herself in the end.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: The Bureau's ambulance is on its way. I'd suggest ending the show and clearing out non-essential personnel to avoid any unnecessary complications, but... I'll leave that for you to decide.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I hope you find yourselves a new ATM. One that wouldn't collapse as easily.

Your jab lands on the manager, but Mimi-meow doesn't react to it at all. It's the mention of the ambulance that cracks her mask open. She looks at Evie. Then, the flicker of hesitation in her eyes quickly turns into something resolute.

Something stirs in you. Is this the kind of expression, the kind of reaction, you'd expect from a self-serving idol who drains everything from those around her? What was she hesitating over, and what did she steel herself for?
Could what lies behind that hesitation... be a turning point?
